key_insight: Bubble curtains in lock-exchange flows exhibit three distinct subregimes within the breakthrough regime, and their behavior depends on both air Froude number and the salt-to-freshwater density ratio.
engineering_relevance: These results provide actionable guidance for tuning bubble curtains to better block salt transport in ship locks and similar hydraulic barriers.
method: Two-phase large-eddy simulations of a laboratory-scale lock-exchange setup
Detailed analysis of flow and density fields around the bubble curtain
Regime classification across varying air Froude number and density ratio
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based identification of three qualitatively distinct subregimes and shows a dependence of salt-blocking effectiveness on the density ratio.
watch_item: Design optimization should not rely on air Froude number alone, because density-ratio effects can change both regime behavior and barrier effectiveness.
paper_title: Lock-exchange flow regimes under low air Froude number bubble curtains
